claims.text: Fluconazole is a triazole antifungal (Diflucan brand)
claims.quote: DIFLUCAN® (fluconazole), the first of a new subclass of synthetic triazole antifungal agents

claims.text: blocks lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase, which converts lanosterol to ergosterol
claims.quote: Fluconazole is a highly selective inhibitor of fungal cytochrome P450 dependent enzyme lanosterol 14-α-demethylase. This enzyme functions to convert lanosterol to ergosterol.

claims.text: loss of normal sterols may be responsible for fungistatic effect
claims.quote: The subsequent loss of normal sterols correlates with the accumulation of 14-α-methyl sterols in fungi and may be responsible for the fungistatic activity of fluconazole.

claims.text: more than 90 percent of an oral dose is absorbed
claims.quote: the bioavailability of orally administered fluconazole is over 90% compared with intravenous administration.

claims.text: plasma half-life about 30 hours (range 20 to 50)
claims.quote: terminal plasma elimination half-life of approximately 30 hours (range: 20 to 50 hours)

claims.text: single 150 mg dose reached vaginal tissue and vaginal fluid
claims.quote: A single oral 150 mg dose of fluconazole administered to 27 patients penetrated into vaginal tissue ... A single oral 150 mg dose of fluconazole administered to 14 patients penetrated into vaginal fluid

claims.text: can be taken with or without food
claims.quote: exposure to the drug is not affected by food. Therefore, DIFLUCAN may be taken without regard to meals.

claims.text: use in pregnancy should be avoided except severe or life-threatening fungal infections, when benefit outweighs risk
claims.quote: Use in pregnancy should be avoided except in patients with severe or potentially life-threatening fungal infections in whom fluconazole may be used if the anticipated benefit outweighs the possible risk to the fetus.

claims.text: epidemiological studies suggest potential risk after 150 mg single or repeated dose in first trimester; limitations, not confirmed in controlled trials
claims.quote: Epidemiological studies suggest a potential risk of spontaneous abortion and congenital abnormalities in infants whose mothers were treated with 150 mg of fluconazole as a single or repeated dose in the first trimester, but these epidemiological studies have limitations

claims.text: findings not confirmed in controlled clinical trials
claims.quote: these findings have not been confirmed in controlled clinical trials.

claims.text: high doses 400 to 800 mg/day during most or all of first trimester: distinct pattern of birth defects
claims.quote: Case reports describe a pattern of distinct congenital anomalies in infants exposed in utero to high dose maternal fluconazole (400 to 800 mg/day) during most or all of the first trimester.

claims.text: low levels in breast milk after single 150 mg dose; caution in nursing woman
claims.quote: Fluconazole was present in low levels in breast milk following administration of a single 150 mg dose ... Caution should be exercised when DIFLUCAN is administered to a nursing woman.

claims.text: side effects 26 percent vs 16 percent intravaginal in U.S. comparative studies
claims.quote: a higher incidence of drug related adverse events with DIFLUCAN (26%) versus intravaginal agents (16%) in U.S. comparative clinical studies.

claims.text: headache 13, nausea 7, abdominal pain 6, diarrhea 3 percent
claims.quote: were headache (13%), nausea (7%), and abdominal pain (6%) ... diarrhea (3%), dyspepsia (1%), dizziness (1%), and taste perversion (1%)

claims.text: rare serious liver reactions; caution with liver dysfunction; stop if liver disease signs
claims.quote: there have been rare cases of serious hepatic reactions during treatment with DIFLUCAN ... DIFLUCAN should be administered with caution to patients with liver dysfunction. DIFLUCAN should be discontinued if clinical signs and symptoms consistent with liver disease develop

claims.text: rare anaphylaxis and angioedema; exfoliative skin disorders
claims.quote: Rarely, angioedema and anaphylactic reaction have been reported in marketing experience. ... Exfoliative skin disorders during treatment with DIFLUCAN have been reported.

claims.text: moderate CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 inhibitor, strong CYP2C19 inhibitor
claims.quote: Fluconazole is a moderate CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 inhibitor. Fluconazole is also a strong inhibitor of CYP2C19.

claims.text: effect persists 4 to 5 days after stopping due to long half-life
claims.quote: The enzyme inhibiting effect of fluconazole persists 4 to 5 days after discontinuation of fluconazole treatment due to the long half-life of fluconazole.

claims.text: warfarin: prothrombin time can rise; monitoring and dose adjustment
claims.quote: Prothrombin time may be increased in patients receiving concomitant DIFLUCAN and coumarin-type anticoagulants. ... Dose adjustment of warfarin may be necessary.

claims.text: statins atorvastatin, simvastatin: myopathy and rhabdomyolysis
claims.quote: The risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis increases when fluconazole is coadministered with HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors metabolized through CYP3A4, such as atorvastatin and simvastatin

claims.text: rare QT prolongation and torsade; erythromycin, pimozide, quinidine contraindicated
claims.quote: there have been rare cases of QT prolongation and torsade de pointes in patients taking fluconazole. ... such as erythromycin, pimozide, and quinidine are contraindicated

claims.text: phenytoin levels rise
claims.quote: DIFLUCAN increases the plasma concentrations of phenytoin.

claims.text: sulfonylureas glipizide, glyburide, tolbutamide levels rise; hypoglycemia
claims.quote: DIFLUCAN reduces the metabolism of tolbutamide, glyburide, and glipizide and increases the plasma concentration of these agents. ... one fatality has been reported from hypoglycemia in association with combined DIFLUCAN and glyburide use.

claims.text: oral contraceptives: EE and LNG up 40 and 24 percent at 200 mg daily; unlikely to affect efficacy
claims.quote: at 200 mg daily, the AUCs of ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel were increased 40% and 24%, respectively. ... multiple-dose use of fluconazole at these doses is unlikely to have an effect on the efficacy of the combined oral contraceptive.

claims.text: single 150 mg oral dose for uncomplicated VVC
claims.quote: Fluconazole 150 mg orally in a single dose

claims.text: OTC intravaginal agents: clotrimazole, miconazole, tioconazole; prescription: butoconazole, terconazole; regimens from single application to 7 to 14 days
claims.quote: Clotrimazole 1% cream 5 g intravaginally daily for 7–14 days ... Tioconazole 6.5% ointment 5 g intravaginally in a single application ... Prescription Intravaginal Agents ... Butoconazole 2% cream ... Terconazole 0.4% cream

claims.text: azole treatment: relief and negative cultures in 80 to 90 percent who complete therapy
claims.quote: Treatment with azoles results in relief of symptoms and negative cultures in 80%–90% of patients who complete therapy.

claims.text: severe VVC: two 150 mg doses 72 hours apart or 7 to 14 days topical
claims.quote: Either 7–14 days of topical azole or 150 mg of fluconazole in two sequential oral doses (second dose 72 hours after initial dose) is recommended.

claims.text: recurrent VVC induction 100/150/200 mg every third day for 3 doses
claims.quote: (e.g., 7–14 days of topical therapy or a 100-mg, 150-mg, or 200-mg oral dose of fluconazole every third day for a total of 3 doses [days 1, 4, and 7]) is recommended

claims.text: maintenance weekly for 6 months
claims.quote: Oral fluconazole (i.e., a 100-mg, 150-mg, or 200-mg dose) weekly for 6 months is the indicated maintenance regimen.

claims.text: recurrent VVC usually three or more episodes in less than a year
claims.quote: usually defined as three or more episodes of symptomatic VVC in <1 year

claims.text: maintenance effective but rarely curative long-term
claims.quote: Suppressive maintenance therapies are effective at controlling recurrent VVC but are rarely curative long-term.

claims.text: pregnancy: only 7-day topical azoles
claims.quote: Only topical azole therapies, applied for 7 days, are recommended for use among pregnant women.

claims.text: single 150 mg dose might be associated with spontaneous abortion and congenital anomalies; should not be used
claims.quote: Epidemiologic studies indicate a single 150-mg dose of fluconazole might be associated with spontaneous abortion and congenital anomalies; therefore, it should not be used.

claims.text: C. glabrata and other non-albicans in 10 to 20 percent of recurrent VVC
claims.quote: C. glabrata and other non–albicans Candida species are observed in 10%–20% of women with recurrent VVC.

claims.text: conventional therapies less effective against non-albicans
claims.quote: Conventional antimycotic therapies are not as effective against these non–albicans yeasts as against C. albicans.

claims.text: culture or PCR for complicated VVC; susceptibility testing if culture positive despite maintenance
claims.quote: Vaginal culture or PCR should be obtained from women with complicated VVC ... susceptibility tests, if available, should be obtained among symptomatic patients who remain culture positive despite maintenance therapy.

claims.text: non-albicans: 7 to 14 days non-fluconazole azole
claims.quote: a longer duration of therapy (7–14 days) with a nonfluconazole azole regimen (oral or topical) is recommended.

claims.text: if recurrence, boric acid 600 mg vaginally once daily for 3 weeks
claims.quote: If recurrence occurs, 600 mg of boric acid in a gelatin capsule administered vaginally once daily for 3 weeks is indicated.

claims.text: persistent symptoms or recurrence within 2 months: evaluate and test; return for follow-up
claims.quote: women with persistent or recurrent symptoms after treatment should be instructed to return for follow-up visits. ... or who has a recurrence of symptoms <2 months after treatment for VVC should be evaluated clinically and tested.

claims.quote: In the evaluation of late clinical cure, there were no significant differences in the odds ratios of success between oral and topical treatment, either as single or multiple-day therapy

claims.text: median time to recurrence 10.2 vs 4.0 months
claims.quote: The median time to clinical recurrence in the fluconazole group was 10.2 months, as compared with 4.0 months in the placebo group

claims.text: long-term cure difficult; benefit wanes after stopping
claims.quote: Long-term weekly treatment with fluconazole can reduce the rate of recurrence of symptomatic vulvovaginal candidiasis. However, a long-term cure remains difficult to achieve.
